title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF NATIONAL EDUCATIONAL COMMISSION
title_original: 국가교육위원회 설치 및 운영에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to provide for matters mandated by the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Education Commission and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

CHAPTER II COMPOSITION, ETC. OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

Article 2 (Criteria for members of the National Education Commission) The qualifications of students, youth, and parents, which are part of the eligibility requirements under Article 3 (2) 5 of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Education Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") for members (hereinafter referred to as "members" in this Chapter) of the National Education Commission under Article 2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "National Education Commission"), shall be classified as follows:
  1. Student: A student who is enrolled in a school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act at the time of commission as a member;
  2. Youth: A person who qualifies as a youth under the Framework Act on Youth at the time of commission as a member;
  3. Parent: A parent whose child is enrolled in a kindergarten under the Early Childhood Education Act, a school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, or a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act at the time of commission as a member.

Article 3 (Organizations related to teachers) (1) “Teachers-related organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 3 (3) 5 of the Act means each of the following organizations:
  1. Teachers' organizations organized in the central government under Article 15 (1) of the Framework Act on Education;
  2. A teachers’ union established nationwide under Article 4 (1) and (2) of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Teachers’ Unions (referring to an associated organization if such an organization is composed of these unions).
  (2) If there are at least 2 teachers-related organizations under paragraph (1), they shall autonomously agree on a nominee when recommending a member under Article 3 (3) 5 of the Act, and if no agreement is reached, nominees shall be determined in the order of the organizations with the largest number of members or union members, with each organization selecting one nominee in turn.
  (3) The National Education Commission may request the head of the relevant central administrative agency or the head of an organization to submit relevant materials or present opinions if it deems it necessary to resolve any disagreement among teachers-related organizations under paragraph (2) regarding the number of members or union members.

Article 4 (Methods of recommendation or nomination of members) A person who intends to recommend or nominate a candidate for appointment or commission as a member under Article 3 (3) 1, 2, and 5 through 7 of the Act shall specify the following matters when making the recommendation or nomination:
  1. Reasons for the recommendation or nomination;
  2. Matters regarding which subparagraph of Article 3 (2) of the Act the recommended or nominated person falls under; in such cases, the recommendation or nomination shall be made based on the criteria specified in the following items:
  a. If a person falls under 2 or more subparagraphs, 1 subparagraph shall be selected;
  b. If the recommended or nominated person holds a position as a teacher, professor, public official, or representative or executive officer who meets any of the eligibility requirements under Article 3 (2) 1 through 4 of the Act at the time of recommendation or nomination, the corresponding subparagraph shall take precedence.

Article 5 (Limitations on profit-making business) No member shall perform the following duties for the purpose of profit-making pursuant to Article 9 (2) of the Act:
  1. Affairs related to the establishment or amendment of the National Education Development Plan, which is deliberated and resolved by the National Education Commission under Article 11 of the Act;
  2. Affairs related to basic matters on the standards and contents of national curricula determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission under Article 12 of the Act;
  3. Affairs related to gathering and coordinating public opinions on education policies, which is conducted by the National Education Commission under Article 13 of the Act.

CHAPTER III ADMINISTRATIVE AFFAIRS OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

Section 1 Formulation of National Education Development Plans and Implementation Plans

Article 6 (Formulation of national educational development plans) (1) The National Education Commission shall establish a national education development plan under Article 10 (1) 1 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "national education development plan") under Article 11 (1) of the Act by March 31 of the year preceding the year in which the plan is implemented.
  (2) A national education development plan shall include the following matters:
  1. Basic objectives and implementation direction of a national education development plan;
  2. Major implementation tasks and methods by period and field (including matters related to early childhood education, elementary and secondary education, higher education, vocational education, and lifelong education);
  3. Scale of resources and measures for securing them for national education development.

Article 7 (Procedures for establishing or amending a national education implementation plan under a national education development plan) (1) The National Education Commission shall prepare guidelines necessary for the head of the relevant central administrative agency and the head of a local government (hereinafter referred to as "heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc.") to establish and formulate an annual implementation plan for their respective duties under a national education development plan (hereinafter referred to as "national education implementation plan") pursuant to Article 11 (5) of the Act and shall notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. by August 31 of the year preceding the year in which the national education implementation plan is implemented.
  (2) The heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. shall formulate a national education implementation plan in accordance with the guidelines under paragraph (1) and submit it to the National Education Commission by December 31 of the year preceding the year in which the plan is implemented.
  (3) The heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. shall promptly submit the amended national education implementation plan to the National Education Commission if they amend the plan submitted under paragraph (2).

Article 8 (Inspection of implementation status and disclosure of results of a national education implementation plan under a national education development plan) (1) The heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. shall prepare the implementation performance of the previous year under Article 11 (6) of the Act and submit it to the National Education Commission by January 31 of the following year.
  (2) The National Education Commission shall inspect the implementation performance submitted under paragraph (1) and notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. of the inspection results by March 31 of the year in which the implementation performance was submitted, and shall post the results on the National Education Commission’s official website.
  (3) The National Education Commission may request the heads of relevant administrative agencies, etc. to submit relevant materials if necessary to inspect the implementation status of a national education implementation plan under Article 11 (7) of the Act.

Section 2 Establishment of Standards and Contents of National Curricula

Article 9 (Standards and contents of national curricula) (1) The National Board of Education shall determine the standards and contents of national curricula under Article 12 (1) of the Act (hereafter in this Section referred to as "national curricula") in consideration of the following matters:
  1. Ensuring equal educational opportunities, autonomy, expertise, and neutrality;
  2. The superintendents of education of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan Cities, Special Self-Governing Cities, Dos, and Special Self-Governing Provinces (hereinafter referred to as "Cities/Dos") shall be able to prepare standards and contents of curricula suitable for regional circumstances;
  3. Autonomy in the operation of curricula of kindergartens under the Early Childhood Education Act and schools under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act shall be respected;
  4. It shall be aligned with the national education development plan;
  5. In establishing or amending the standards and contents of national curricula, the public participation shall be guaranteed and the process shall be disclosed to the public.
  (2) The standards and contents of national curricula shall include the following matters:
  1. Matters on the principles of composition and the system of national curricula;
  2. Matters on the areas and contents of the curriculum for kindergartens under the Early Childhood Education Act;
  3. Matters on the areas, contents, organization, and criteria for the allocation of instructional hours in the curricula of schools under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.

Article 10 (Establishment and amendment of standards and contents of national curricula) (1) If the National Education Commission deems it necessary to establish or amend the standards and contents of the national curricula in consideration of the establishment of a national education development plan, changes in the educational environment, and other factors under Article 12 (1) of the Act, it shall determine the standards and contents of the national curricula through deliberation and resolution by the National Education Commission.
  (2) When determining the standards and contents of the national curricula under paragraph (1), the National Education Commission shall deliberate and resolve whether to proceed with the establishment or amendment if there is a request falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
  1. When the Minister of Education requests the establishment of new standards and contents of the national curricula or the amendment of the existing standards and contents in consideration of new educational demands, etc.;
  2. When the council of superintendents of education under Article 42 (1) of the Local Education Autonomy Act requests the establishment of new standards and contents of the national curricula or the amendment of the existing standards and contents with the consent of a majority of the superintendents of education of Cities/Dos;
  3. When at least 200,000 people agree within 30 days from the date of posting on the National Education Commission’s official website or other platforms under Article 13 (1) regarding the establishment or amendment of the standards and contents of national curricula.
  (3) The National Education Commission shall notify the requesting institution, etc. of the deliberation and resolution results under paragraph (2) within 90 days from the date the request is made under each subparagraph of that paragraph (in the case of subparagraph 3 of that paragraph, from the date 30 days after the public opinion is posted); provided, if the deliberation and resolution cannot be completed within that period due to unavoidable circumstances, the period may be extended by up to 60 days.
  (4) When the National Education Commission intends to establish or amend the standards and contents of national curricula, it shall formulate a plan in advance that includes the implementation schedule, details, and applicable subjects, and finalize it through deliberation and resolution by the National Education Commission.
  (5) The National Education Commission shall promptly post the finalized plan under paragraph (4) on its official website.
  (6) When deliberating and resolving matters on the establishment or amendment of the standards and contents of national curricula under paragraphs (1), (2), and (4), the National Education Commission shall seek the opinions of the national curriculum monitoring group under Article 12 (1) and the preliminary review opinions of the expert committee under Article 18 (1) 2.

Article 11 (Research, analysis, and inspection of national curricula) (1) The National Education Commission shall establish an annual implementation plan for the research, analysis, and inspection of the national curricula under Article 12 (2) of the Act.
  (2) The National Education Commission shall promptly post the results of the research, analysis, and inspection of the national curricula conducted under Article 12 (2) of the Act on its official website.

Article 12 (National curriculum monitoring group) (1) The National Education Commission may establish a national curriculum monitoring group (hereinafter referred to as "national curriculum monitoring group") to collect public opinions on the standards and contents of national curricula under Article 12 (1) of the Act and to support the research, analysis, and inspection of national curricula under paragraph (2) of that Article.
  (2) A national curriculum monitoring group may be operated by classification based on offices of education of Cities/Dos, school levels, and subject areas.
  (3) Members of national curriculum monitoring groups shall be commissioned by the Chairperson of the National Education Commission from among the following persons:
  1. Teachers under Article 20 (1) of the Early Childhood Education Act or Article 19 (1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
  2. Students enrolled in a school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act or a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
  3. Parents under subparagraph 3 of Article 2;
  4. Education experts, education administrators, figures from various sectors of society with extensive expertise and experience in the field of education, or persons affiliated with a non-profit, non-governmental organization under the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act.
  (4) The Chairperson of the National Education Commission may provide training at least once a year to the members commissioned under paragraph (3) to support the performance of their duties.
  (5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the national curriculum monitoring group, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission.

Section 3 Collection and Coordination of Public Opinions on Education Policies

Article 13 (Procedures for the collection and coordination of public opinions on education policies) (1) The National Education Commission shall take necessary measures to allow the public to post opinions on education policies or indicate their agreement or disagreement on the National Education Commission’s official website or other platforms in order to collect public opinions under Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act.
  (2) "Where there is a request from at least a certain number of citizens prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act means a case where at least 100,000 people agree within 90 days from the date a public opinion is posted on the National Education Commission’s official website or other platforms under paragraph (1).
  (3) When deliberating and resolving whether to proceed with the procedures for the collection and coordination of public opinions under Article 13 (2) of the Act, the National Education Commission shall notify the requesting institution, etc. of the result within 45 days from the date the request is received (in the case of Article 13 (1) 2 of the Act, from the date 90 days have passed since the public opinion was posted).

Article 14 (Submission of implementation plan on results of collecting and coordinating public opinions) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, and other heads of relevant institutions (hereinafter referred to as "heads of relevant agencies, etc.") who have been notified of the results of processing the collection and coordination of public opinions under Article 13 (3) of the Act shall establish an implementation plan based on the results and submit it to the National Education Commission within 30 days from the date they are notified of the results (in cases where a request for reconsideration has been made under paragraph (4) of that Article, within 30 days from the date they are notified of the reconsideration results under Article 15 (2)).

Article 15 (Procedures for re-deliberation of results of collecting and coordinating public opinions) (1) When requesting re-deliberation from the National Education Commission under Article 13 (4) of the Act, the heads of relevant institutions, etc. shall submit a written request for re-deliberation specifying the detailed reasons for the request to the National Education Commission within 30 days from the date they are notified of the processing results.
  (2) The National Education Commission shall notify the heads of relevant institutions, etc. who requested the re-deliberation of the results within 60 days from the date the request under paragraph (1) is received; provided, if there are unavoidable circumstances, the period may be extended by up to 30 days.
  (3) No further request for deliberation may be made regarding the results of the re-deliberation notified by the National Education Commission under paragraph (2).
  (4) Matters necessary for the collection and coordination of public opinions on education policies, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission.

Section 4 Consultative Body of Stakeholders in Education Policies

Article 16 (Composition and operation of consultative body of stakeholders in education policies) (1) Pursuant to Article 14 (2) of the Act, a consultative body of stakeholders in education policies (hereinafter referred to as the "education policy consultative body") shall be established within the National Education Commission to consult with relevant central administrative agencies and local governments on the following matters:
  1. Matters on the establishment, amendment, and inspection of the implementation of national education development plans and national education implementation plans;
  2. Matters on the public notification of the standards and contents of national curricula under Article 12 of the Act and the inspection of national curricula;
  3. Matters on the implementation of the results of collecting and coordinating public opinions on education policies under Article 13 of the Act;
  4. Other matters related to education policies that require consultation with relevant central administrative agencies and local governments.
  (2) The chairperson of the education policy consultative body shall be the Secretary General of the National Education Commission under Article 20 (2) of the Act, and the members of the education policy consultative body shall be as follows:
  1. A public official belonging to the Senior Executive Service of a relevant central administrative agency who is nominated by the head of the respective agency;
  2. A public official at the director-general level or higher of a City/Do who is nominated by the Special Metropolitan Mayor, a Metropolitan Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor;
  3. A public official at the director-general level or higher of a City/Do office of education who is nominated by the superintendent of education.
  (3) Meetings of the education policy consultative body shall be convened by the chairperson when the chairperson deems it necessary to consult with relevant central administrative agencies and local governments.
  (4) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the education policy consultative body, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be determined by the Chairperson of the National Education Commission through a resolution of the National Education Commission.

CHAPTER IV OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL EDUCATION COMMISSION

Article 17 (Composition and operation of the Civil Participation Committee) (1) The Civil Participation Committee under Article 16 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Civil Participation Committee") shall be composed of up to 500 members, including one chairperson.
  (2) The members of the Civil Participation Committee shall be commissioned by the chairperson of the National Education Commission from among the following persons; in such cases, the members under subparagraph 1 shall constitute at least 3/5 of the total number of members of the Civil Participation Committee:
  1. Citizens who wish to participate in the advisory affairs of the Civil Participation Committee and are selected through the recruitment process determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission;
  2. Persons with extensive expertise and experience in various fields such as education, culture, media, employment, industry, welfare, and science and technology, who are recommended by the Special Metropolitan Mayor, a Metropolitan Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, a Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or a superintendent of education of a City/Do.
  (3) The term of office for the commissioned members under paragraph (2) shall be 2 years, and they may be reappointed only once; provided, if a new member is commissioned due to the resignation of a member of the Civil Participation Committee or other reasons, the term of office shall be the remaining period of the predecessor’s term.
  (4) Meetings of the Civil Participation Committee shall be convened by the chairperson of the Civil Participation Committee when the chairperson deems it necessary to collect public opinions.
  (5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Civil Participation Committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission.

Article 18 (Composition and operation of expert committees) (1) The expert committee under Article 17 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "expert committee") shall be composed according to the following classifications:
  1. An expert committee for providing advice or conducting preliminary reviews on the affairs under Article 10 (1) 1, 3, or 4 of the Act: Up to 21 members, including one chairperson;
  2. An expert committee for providing advice or conducting preliminary reviews on the affairs under Article 10 (1) 2 of the Act: Up to 45 members, including one chairperson.
  (2) The members of the expert committee shall be commissioned by the chairperson of the National Education Commission from among those with extensive expertise and experience in the field of education, with the consent of a majority of the incumbent members of the National Education Commission, in consideration of gender.
  (3) The term of office for the members under paragraph (2) shall be 2 years, and they may be reappointed only once.
  (4) Meetings of the expert committee shall be convened by the chairperson of each expert committee when the chairperson deems it necessary to provide practical advice on the affairs under the jurisdiction of the National Education Commission or to conduct preliminary reviews on matters subject to deliberation and resolution.
  (5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the expert committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be determined by the chairperson of the National Education Commission through a resolution of the National Education Commission.

Article 19 (Composition and operation of special committee) (1) A special committee under Article 18 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "special committee") shall be comprised of not more than 21 members, including one chairperson.
  (2) The chairperson of a special committee shall be designated by the chairperson of the National Education Commission from among the members of the special committee under paragraph (3).
  (3) The members of a special committee shall be commissioned by the Chairperson of the National Education Commission from among those with extensive expertise and experience in the field of education, in consideration of gender.
  (4) Matters necessary for the composition of the special committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be determined by the Chairperson of the National Education Commission through a resolution of the National Education Commission.

Article 20 (Qualifications of expert members) (1) Expert members under Article 19 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "expert members") shall be commissioned by the Chairperson of the National Education Commission from among those who hold a doctoral degree in a field related to education, culture, media, employment, industry, welfare, or science and technology, or those recognized as having equivalent expertise and experience, in consideration of gender.
  (2) The term of office of expert members shall be 2 years.

Article 21 (Dismissal of members) If a member of the Civil Participation Committee, a member of an expert committee, a member of a special committee, or an expert member (hereinafter referred to as "member, etc." in this Article) falls under any of the following cases, the Chairperson of the National Education Commission may dismiss the member, etc.:
  1. Where he or she becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a mental or physical disorder;
  2. If he or she has committed any misconduct in connection with his or her duties;
  3. Where he or she is deemed unsuitable as a member, etc. due to neglect of duties, injury to dignity, or other reasons;
  4. Where the member, etc. voluntarily declares that he or she is unable to perform his or her duties.

Article 22 (Designation of education research centers) (1) The National Education Commission may designate an education research center under Article 21 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "education research center") from among the institutions or corporations falling under any of the following subparagraphs through a resolution of the National Education Commission:
  1. National and public research institutes;
  2. A research Institute funded by the State or a local government;
  3. Schools under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
  4. A research institute which is a non-profit corporation under Article 32 of the Civil Act;
  5. A research institute that is a corporation (excluding a for-profit corporation) established under a special Act.
  (2) The standards for designating education research centers shall be as follows:
  1. It shall have a dedicated organization and personnel to support the affairs of the National Education Commission;
  2. It shall have the necessary facilities to carry out tasks supporting the affairs of the National Education Commission;
  3. It shall have an appropriate business plan for performing its duties as an education research center.
  (3) An institution or corporation that intends to be designated as an education research center under paragraph (1) shall submit an application for designation to the National Education Commission along with the following documents:
  1.Current status or plans to secure a dedicated organization and personnel for performing affairs;
  2. Status of possession or plans for securing facilities necessary for performing duties;
  3. A business plan and operational regulations for the performance of affairs.
  (4) When the National Education Commission designates an education research center, it shall post the designation on the official website of the National Education Commission.
  (5) Matters necessary for the designation of an education research center, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be determined and publicly notified by the National Education Commission.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 32627, May 9, 2022>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on July 21, 2022.
Article 2 (Applicability to amended standards and contents of national curricula publicly notified by the Minister of Education)
Articles 9 and 10 shall not apply to national curricula for elementary and secondary schools amended and publicly notified by the Minister of Education by December 31, 2022, under Article 4 of Addenda of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Education Commission (Act No. 18298).
Article 3 Omitted.
